arguments.evidence: A prose: "measured energy ranks P2 lowest at 15 kWh, then P3 at 24, P1 at 44 and P4 at 64, so P2 is the client-correct selection, with successive gaps of 9, 20 and 20 kWh." B independently recomputes: "Recomputed ladder: P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh," all qualify (quality 95/91/100/88 ≥80; defects 1/3/3/5 ≤5). Table confirms P2 energy 15 = unique minimum. No visible callout or bar feature in either page set singles out a non-client candidate; both recommend P2. Ballot P2 follows client policy.

persuasion.evidence_that_changed_my_view: No change: my initial round-5 judgment was P2; A's brief and B's memo both recompute the ladder from the trusted table and arrive at P2 independently, so the artifacts match my client-correct reasoning.
persuasion.residual_concern: Left bar charts in both delivered page sets cannot be pixel-verified at this rendering; rounds 3-4 showed off-scale left figures. Prose governs; my own figure should use a stated fixed scale.
persuasion.strongest_counterargument: P4 sits exactly at the five-defect ceiling with zero spare slots, and the 9 kWh P2-P3 margin is the smallest gap, so the selection is least robust to a measurement revision.

This round I can't compute scale precisely from thumbnails, but I can note apparent consistency. B's left chart shows one tall bar (red?) and others small — hmm.

I'll record honestly: at delivered rendering, bar heights appear broadly consistent with the ladder; I cannot confirm exact px scale.

Make the call. One function call, then stop.
